activities.title: Samba & Candombe Movement Foundations
activities.description: Feel empowered with this unique women's only movement class! Learn authentic Samba from Brazil, Candombe from Uruguay, and more. The focus is not only on learning steps, but on discovering how to move your body within each step while connecting to the music in a natural and expressive way. The focus is on foundation and to move with intention while learning these beautiful dances. As you develop rhythm, coordination, posture, and confidence while exploring a variety of movements - hips, torso, shoulder and more - you will also dive into the cultural roots behind each dance. Learn, smile, and move like never before and become part of a welcoming supportive community. Wear loose comfortable clothes, an option to dance in bare feet or indoor shoes and bring a water bottle! activities.title: Tai Chi with Wang Heng - 24 Form
activities.description: Long term Tai Chi practice can help improve mood and emotional states, enhance body shape and reduce fat. The results of many scientific studies show that Health Qi Gong can improve the functions of the cardiovascular, respiratory and digestive systems, enhance balancing ability, better the flexibility and force of muscles, improve mood, and lessen anxiety and stress. $10.00. No session April 10 and June 19.

activities.title: Tai Chi with Wang Heng - Sword 32 Form
activities.description: Tai Chi Sword is a form of Tai Chi quan in which the sword is considered an extension of the body. The integration helps to direct body energy through the sword and produce movements that are smooth and graceful. Instructor can provide wushu swords to train with. Drop-in $11.

activities.description:
Join us for some high-energy volleyball action! Whether you’re looking to stay active, meet new people, or just enjoy some friendly competition, our program is the perfect place to bump, set, and spike your way to a great time. This program is designed for players who already know the basics, so bring your skills and get ready to play!

Each session is capped at 28 participants, consisting of 24 registered participants and 4 guaranteed drop-in spots. When at full capacity, one substitute rotation will be implemented per court.

Important registration & drop-in details:

activities.title: Qigong (Free Trial Program)
activities.description: Medical Qigong is an ancient branch of Traditional Chinese Medicine focused on health preservation and longevity. Through the posture, breath, and mental focus—students learn to purge toxins, tonify organs and regulate life force energy - Qi. By integrating physical movement with creative visualization, these exercises empower you to restore balance to your physical, emotional, and spiritual well-being. No class Oct 15 & 22.

activities.title: Handpan (Hang drum) Private lessons
activities.description: Discover the soothing, meditative sound of the Handpan in this beginner-friendly music program. Students will learn proper playing techniques, rhythmic patterns, and expressive improvisation on this unique steel instrument. No musical background is required. Guided by an experienced Handpan performer and instructor, participants will explore creativity, reduce stress, and enjoy a welcoming, supportive learning environment. Instruments will be provided. activities.description: Discover the creativity and confidence that comes with learning to sew! Designed for youth ages 13-18, this beginner-friendly program teaches the fundamentals of machine sewing in a fun, supportive environment. Participants will learn sewing machine operation, fabric selection and handling, measuring, cutting, garment construction, and professional finishing techniques while completing problem-solving abilities, and valuable lifelong sewing skills they can use for clothing repairs, fashion, and future creative projects. activities.title: everyBODYoga with Klara Kroupa
activities.description:
This all-levels class is designed to increase strength and flexibility, as well as stamina and resilience.

Exercises are specific to target the often forgotten, small muscles and joints that are crucial to maintain support & alignment within the body as well as ensuring sustained mobility as we age. We all want to keep enjoying all the sports and activities we’ve always been used to doing – so paying attention to posture, core, lower back, hips, knees, shoulders, neck, feet … is vital.

The class can be as challenging as you wish to make it. Step-by-step instruction is offered to set-up the foundation and form for each movement. Modifications are also offered to ensure a safe and rewarding experience for any level of yogi - from beginner to elite athlete. The use of props (blocks, strap, bolster, cushions, etc) is always encouraged to not only enhance poses, but to also provide support and safety.

activities.title: Personal Safety & Self Protection Workshop
activities.description:
Your Personal Safety is a PRIORITY. Experiencing fear, apprehension and worrying about your safety walking down the street is a way of life now for many. It doesn’t have to be. Random unprovoked assaults in the greater Vancouver area is at an all time high according to the statistics provided by the Vancouver Police Department. Predators have a finely tuned radar for vulnerability. This Personal Protection program is one of the world’s best personal safety and self empowering program with actionable tools you can use immediately. Change your entire presence from “potential target” to “not worth the trouble”. And when you carry yourself with the quiet confidence that only comes from knowing exactly how to handle potential threats…they will more likely walk away. Anyone regardless of age, size or fitness capacity can learn this along with the proper tactical skills to deploy if needed. Reduce your risk of being an easy target. Empowerment comes from education and principles of safety, not choreographed fancy moves. Avoid, de-escalate and disengaging from a threat are fundamentals of this course. Your body has all the tools you need. Be your own bodyguard.Your personal safety matters to me.
Go to: https://kravmagaforcefire.com/ [kravmagaforcefire.com] for more information.

activities.title: Tai Chi - Traditional Yang Style 108 Form - Part One
activities.description: Tai Chi (taijiquan) is an "internal" style of Chinese martial arts, based on the principle of the interplay of Yin and Yang. The slow and graceful movements of Tai Chi promote the flow of Qi though the body, and promote mental and physical balance. The Yang style is named for the family that developed this particular lineage, and is the most widely practiced style of Tai Chi in the world. Characterized by broad, open strokes, slow, even movements, and an upright posture, the traditional form (also known as the "long form") takes anywhere from 20 to 40 minutes to perform. In this course, we will study the first third, or so, of the sequence. Learning the entire form will take about one year. Drop-in $19, if space permits. No session Nov 10

Drawing from Qigong, Taijiquan and contemporary dance, the programme develops proprioception, postural stability and fluid adaptability through joyful, improvisational movement. Emphasis is placed on ease of movement rather than on fear-driven fall avoidance.The programme is offered in three modules, each lasting 10 weeks:Module 1 - Standing foundationsModule 2 - Sitting and kneeling dynamicsModule 3 - Lying and rolling integrationEach module may be taken on its own as a complete and meaningful experience, or joined sequentially as a progressive series that gradually increases physical challenge and movement complexity. This flexible structure makes the program suitable for a wide range of participants, including those new to movement-based therapy or those seeking a year-long exploration of confident embodied movement. No Class: Sep 30 and Nov 11

activities.title: Athletic Interval Training
activities.description: This high-intensity fitness class combines strength training, cardiovascular conditioning, and core work for a full-body workout. Refine your weight training technique while improving overall fitness. Participants are expected to be able to work at a high intensity in a continuous group fitness environment. This class requires completion of the PAR-Q+ health screening at eparmedx.com prior to participation. This supports safe participation and helps identify whether medical clearance or an appropriate alternative class is recommended. Drop-in $12.

activities.title: Flow Yoga
activities.description: This intermediate-level yoga class is a dynamic and physically engaging practice focusing on alignment, flexibility, posture, balance, and body awareness. We begin with foam rolling to release tension and enhance mobility, then flow through a series of yoga poses guided by breath, finishing with deep stretching and a 5-minute Savasana. Participants are expected to be comfortable moving through a continuous, moderately paced yoga practice that includes standing, floor-based, and balance postures. This class requires completion of the PAR-Q+ health screening at eparmedx.com prior to participation. This supports safe participation and helps identify whether medical clearance or an appropriate alternative class is recommended. Drop-in $12. No session Oct 12.

activities.title: Mat Pilates
activities.description: This intermediate-level, physically challenging class offers a series of classical Pilates exercises guided by breath and clear cueing to strengthen your core and whole body. Improve posture, flexibility, and coordination for greater ease in daily movement. Class begins with 25 minutes of foam rolling for myofascial release. Participants are expected to be comfortable with floor-based movement, core engagement, and working at a continuous moderate pace. This class requires completion of the PAR-Q+ health screening at eparmedx.com and a signed waiver prior to participation. These help identify whether medical clearance or an alternative class is recommended. Drop-in $12. No session Sep 20.

activities.title: Pilates Yoga Fusion
activities.description: We will start with 25 minutes of myofascial release using foam rollers, followed by 20 minutes of traditional Pilates, 20 minutes of flow yoga, and finish with a 5-minute Savasana. This efficient 3-in-1 class improves core strength, posture, balance, flexibility, and body awareness while enhancing overall well-being. Please arrive at least 5 minutes early to set up your mat and equipment. Class starts promptly at 5:30 PM. Participants are expected to be comfortable transitioning between standing, floor-based, and flowing movement in a continuous class format. This class requires completion of the PAR-Q+ health screening at eparmedx.com and a signed waiver prior to participation. These help identify whether medical clearance or an alternative class is recommended. Drop-in $12.

activities.title: Tai Chi - 24 Form (suitable for beginners)
activities.description: Tai Chi (Taiji or Taijiquan) is a Chinese martial art based on the principle of the interplay of Yin and Yang. The slow and graceful movements of Tai Chi promote the circulation of Qi, or vital essence, through the body, and have been shown to improve balance, coordination, and concentration. The 24 Form, or "simplified Yang style," is a short routine perfect for beginners. Drop in $20. No session Nov 10.

activities.title: Qigong
activities.description: Qi is energy. Gong means skills acquired through training. Loosely translated, Qigong is energy work. There are countless forms of Qigong training from Chinese medicine, martial arts, and Buddhist and Taoist traditions. Some forms involve more movement, others emphasize stillness. Visualization, breathing techniques, sound, pressure point massage, posture and movement are examples of methods used to build, circulate, emit, and absorb Qi for health and well-being. Drop-in $20. No session Nov 10.

activities.title: Circle of Life Reiki
activities.description:
Are you seeking clarity and insight in areas such as money, relationships, success, love, communication, intuition, and your connection with the life around you? This is the perfect place to begin. In this gentle introduction to Circle of Life Reiki, we will focus on one chakra each week, exploring how it relates to each key area of life, its unique lessons, receiving Reiki energy activation, and engaging in chakra-balancing activities. Circle of Life Reiki is a newest high-frequency energy designed to help you connect deeply with your own nature and the world around you. Join Reiki Master Shehbaz for guided meditations and rejuvenating energy experiences that nurture the soul and awaken a profound sense of peace, joy, and vitality. You’ll be invited to sit comfortably in a chair or lie on a provided yoga mat while soothing music plays in the background. No prior experience is needed. This class does not include hands-on healing and does not certify you as a Reiki practitioner; it is a space for rest, renewal, and gentle self-discovery. Completing all seven sessions can leave you feeling more balanced, refreshed, and energized. If you’ve been craving deep relaxation and a sense of belonging, this program is a beautiful way to invite fresh energy into your life.
Class Notes: Please come with an open heart, ready to receive deep healing and relaxation. Plan for a quiet, restful evening afterward and enjoy a nourishing meal or snack when you return home. You’re welcome to bring a pillow or blanket for extra comfort and coziness.

activities.title: Gentle Yoga - Set 1
activities.description: Open to all fitness levels, everyone can do this class with confidence, learning how to practice yoga postures safely. activities.title: Intermediate Yoga
activities.description: This class is crafted for students interested in building a solid foundation in yoga postures and the breath-body connection. Through the mindful use of props, students will be safely guided to refine their practice, allowing for greater access to these challenging poses. This class will strengthen, open, and energize, encouraging students to expand both their physical skills and their inner resilience. Drop-in $16/Adult, $13/Senior.

activities.title: Darkroom: Introduction to the Basics
activities.description: This course will take you through the process of developing film and making traditional wet prints from negatives using black and white photographic materials. It is an introductory course, enabling the student to grasp the fundamentals of processing, chemicals, darkroom safety and enlarging. Over the course of the program you will develop one rolls of film, make a contact sheet and create quality silver gelatin prints. The course requires additional materials, which will cost from $50 to $100. A list will be provided at the beginning of your first class. You will also need to have an exposed roll of black and white film (excluding Ilford XP2) in either 35mm or 120 format for the first day of class.

activities.title: PICKLEBALL STAGE 2/STAGE 3: ATTACK OR RESET
activities.description:
Not every ball should be attacked. In this class, you’ll learn how to recognize attacking opportunities, when to slow the game down, and how to make high-percentage shots at the kitchen line. Learn how to use both attacking volleys & resets to gain control of the rally – more rallies & less unforced errors. It is NOT necessary to purchase a paddle for this class. Paddles, balls & equipment will be provided. If you are unable to make the first day, please text Coach Mona at 778-908-2878.

Drop-in $28, space and instructor permitting.

Discover when and why to use each shot to outsmart your opponents. It is NOT necessary to purchase a paddle for this class. Paddles, balls & all equipment will be provided. If you are unable to make the first day, please text Coach Mona at 778-908-2878

Drop-in $28, space and instructor permitting.

activities.title: Candlelit Yin Yoga
activities.description: A slow paced meditative practice, designed to deeply open the body and support connective tissue, joint, and fascia health. Guided in a candlelit setting, this class uses long-held postures and mindful breathwork in restoring the energy flow within the body and promoting flexibility, joint mobility, and relaxation. All levels of yoga are welcome. Modifications and guided use of props, breathwork, and mediation will be provided. Drop-in $20 (space permitting). No class Nov 11, 25.

activities.title: Preteen Pro D Camp - Pumpkin Patch
activities.description:
Come spend your pro d day at the pumpkin patch and take home your very own pumpkin! Please note this program is rain or shine and includes the use of public transportation. In the event of inclement weather, the activity may change but participants will be notified in advance. Pumpkin patch information will be included in the parent email once local pumpkin patches release their schedules. Parents/Guardians will receive an email with the Parent Communication/Policy manual and forms before camp, detailing camp expectations and guidelines. Participants must be between the ages of 10-13, to register for camp.
This day camp is held in the False Creek Community Centre Lounge and offsite (out trip). The sensory environment may include loud noises, bright lights, or crowded spaces. Staff prepare a daily visual schedule to help campers know what to expect for the day. Sensory resource kits may be available, including noise-canceling headphones, sunglasses, fidget tools, and visual aids. The day camp space includes a chill-out zone and a low-sensory area, with staff working to provide quiet breaks in low-stimulation zones.
Program staff are typically post-secondary students with diverse interests and levels of experience, and generally between 18 and 22 years old. This program has a staff-to-participant ratio of 1:10, with additional support from youth volunteers.
Please reach out to us at the time of registration if your child needs more leader attention and support in order to participate in camp. Please call the centre to inform staff if your child will be bringing an additional support person as a cleared Police Information Check is required for this person.
Please pack a healthy lunch, snack and water and wear activity appropriate attire. Be mindful that we have limited spots. NOTE: Day camps require 14 days notice for a full refund.

activities.title: Mochi Mooncake Making Workshop
activities.description: Celebrate Mid-Autumn Festival by making your own mochi mooncakes from scratch — no baking required. In this hands-on workshop, participants learn to make the delicate glutinous rice snow-skin dough, then shape and fill each mooncake with red bean, strawberry, or milky custard before pressing them with traditional wooden molds. Each participant takes home a box of finished mooncakes plus a recipe card to recreate them at home. Suitable for all skill levels — no cooking experience required. All materials will be provided. Led by Abraham Wong, a Hong Kong-born, Vancouver-based chef featured by CBC Vancouver for his Mid-Autumn mooncake teaching. Registration only, no drop-ins.

activities.title: Kitsilano MS Support Group
activities.description:
The Kitsilano Community Centre has a long and fruitful relationship with the Multiple Sclerosis community. Currently they host a drop-in self-help group for people with MS from all over the lower mainland every Friday afternoon, statutory holidays excluded.We try to meet at the Community Centre as much as possible but when we can’t we still meet via Zoom or do a combined Zoom and in person event. We have a diverse membership, people of all ages are welcome and we believe in a barrier free experience. We come together, to share, gasp, laugh and especially to listen. We believe that no one should be on this journey alone. We start most sessions with a quick chat and have a roundtable where everyone has a chance to speak. Sometimes we bring in guests. We have a few social events over the year including a summer picnic and Christmas luncheon off the premises. We also do some philanthropic events such as the MS Walk and other charitable endeavors. If this seems like something you would like to experience and have some questions, please please contact the navigator at the BC Yukon MS Society at 604-689-3144.
Please note: Socials, events and volunteer work outside of the Support Group meeting time at Kitsilano CC are not associated with the KCCA, Vancouver Park Board & COV, and operate independently.

activities.title: Qigong
activities.description:
Qi is “energy.” Gong is “skill acquired through training.” Hence, Qigong is energy cultivation training. There are many techniques to cultivate the internal energy of the body, from Taoist, Buddhist, martial arts, and Chinese medicine traditions. Various methods include movement, posture, breath work, visualization, sound, massage, etc., all with the purpose of building and regulating the Qi in the body for physical and mental well-being.

The slow and graceful movements of Tai Chi promote the circulation of Qi, or vital essence, through the body, and have been shown to improve balance, coordination, and concentration. The 24 Form, or "simplified Yang style," is a short routine perfect for beginners.

activities.title: Dynamic Baby - Infant Development
activities.description: Movement develops the brain! We will spend time moving together finding moments of grounding, flow, ease, strength and play while learning how to facilitate effective cues to nurture your baby’s self-perception, use of expression and efficiency in movement. The developmental milestones incorporate rolling, creeping, crawling and locomoting with additional movement explorations that will harness full body connectivity. The last third of the class will focus on handling skills that caregivers can utilize to support their infant’s ability to self-regulate enriching their child’s independence. Please wear comfortable clothes you can move in and bring a blanket and three toys the infant can handle. No drop ins. Please refer to my website for more information on Infant Developmental Movement Education: Natashamartina.com or my Instagram page - @infantmovementplayground

activities.description: Movement develops the brain! We will spend time moving together finding moments of grounding, flow, ease, strength and play while learning how to facilitate effective cues to nurture your baby’s self-perception, use of expression and efficiency in movement. The developmental milestones incorporate rolling, creeping, crawling and locomoting with additional movement explorations that will harness full body connectivity. The last third of the class will focus on handling skills that caregivers can utilize to support their infant’s ability to self-regulate enriching their child’s independence. Please wear comfortable clothes you can move in and bring a blanket and three toys the infant can handle. No drop ins. Please refer to my website for more information on Infant Developmental Movement Education: Natashamartina.com or my Instagram page - @infantmovementplayground. No session Nov 10.

activities.title: Petit Architect Pro-D Camp: Build a Haunted House
activities.description: Get ready for a frightfully fun STEAM adventure! In this spooky hands-on workshop, kids ages 7-12 will become architects of the strange and unusual as they design and build their very own haunted house. Campers will explore creative design ideas inspired by mysterious Halloween spaces, sketch and plan eerie rooms like vampire lairs, witch kitchens, ghost hideouts, secret passageways, and monster laboratories, build a detailed 3D haunted house model using cardboard, recycled materials, and craft supplies, and problem-solve like real designers: how can they make their haunted house spooky and structurally strong? By the end of the workshop, each camper will have a one-of-a-kind haunted house model and a spooky new appreciation for architecture and creative design. No experience needed, just bring your imagination and your Halloween spirit! Perfect for: Halloween lovers, creative builders, imaginative storytellers, and kids who love spooky fun!

activities.title: BCRPA Choose to Move - Info Session
activities.description:
Join Choose to Move to help introduce the habit of physical activity into your daily life in ways that make sense for you. Choose to Move is free and flexible, and provides you with motivation and support to become more active. In Choose to Move, you receive both individual and group support. You will work with a trained activity coach to develop and stick to a physical activity plan made just for you. You choose activities that you know you will enjoy and are able to do! You will also join a group of other Choose to Movers to share successes and challenges.With the help of your activity coach and support group, you will find the motivation and accountability you need to achieve your goals.
To learn more about Choose to Move visit www.choosetomove.ca.
Participants must attend the Choose to Move Information Session to be eligible for the program

activities.title: BCRPA ActivAge 1 Functional Fitness/Adaptable Skills
activities.description:
ActivAge™ is a free 3-month group-led physical activity program for inactive older adults. It introduces participants to physical activity and reinforces their commitment to incorporate it into their daily lives.

The program is progressive with planned physical activities (stretching, activity, and cool-down) based on ActivAge™ training. This fun and social program will help get participants moving in a relaxed environment with likeminded people.

The program focuses on improving activities associated with daily living, strengthening muscles used day-to-day (ie: bending, lifting, stretching, etc).

Each class incorporates physical activities that engage participants, and features in-class discussions and resources to improve overall health and physical well-being.

activities.description: Changing Aging is an evidence-based exercise program for older adults (55+ years) delivered by specially trained UBC BodyWorks School of Kinesiology student instructors. It focuses on strength, mobility, and cardiovascular health through muscle and bone strengthening exercises followed by intervals of aerobic exercise. Fitness assessments are offered at the start and end of the program in order to monitor your progress. An initial assessment at UBC is required to join the program, with follow-up assessments annually. activities.title: Indigenous Beading Class for Adults
activities.description:
Tansi! (Hi in Cree) Learn Indigenous Beading with Gigi a Woodland Cree, (Nihithaw) Osage, (Wazhazhe) and Two Spirit Artist. This class will:

Introduce you to the trading of different beads from cultures and the history of seed beads, shell beads, and glass beads.

Make a beaded floral rosette and the class will be able to choose which colour combinations they want and a choice of seed or glass beads.

You will also bead orange shirt pins for Residential School awareness.

Choose your own design to bead for a keychain. No sess Oct 10.

activities.title: The Natural Way to Draw
activities.description:
Bring your world to life using the tool you already have: your eyes. Skip the rulers, grids, and lengthy preparation to learn a remarkably effective way to translate what you see onto paper. This approach aligns how you naturally see with a relaxed, fluid way to draw, making it easy to capture your subjects with organic accuracy and fewer corrections. Students are required to bring their own supplies. A concise supply list will be emailed to participants.

This course is designed for anyone who has always wanted to draw without enduring long dry lectures and technical theory. With this practical approach, you will capture the essence of any subject quickly, bypassing the need for any perfection or tedious shading.

Broderick Wong is an artist and educator who demystifies drawing rules so they actually click. Known for capturing striking realism, his hands-on approach helps you bypass perfectionism and draw naturally from day one. www.broderickwongart.com

activities.title: Watercolour Made Simple
activities.description:
Experience a modern, simplified approach to watercolor painting. You’ll skip the heavy theory and exhausting three-hour sessions, jumping straight into hands-on painting. Using minimal supplies, traceable templates, and gradual, bite-sized lessons, this course makes watercolor simple, predictable, and incredibly fun. Best of all, you'll walk away with a painting you can be proud of, every single week. No class Sept 30.

This course is designed for anyone who has always wanted to try watercolors without the long lectures or overloading on theory. If you want a no-fluff approach that makes painting feel approachable, achievable and relaxing, while building your skills from day one, this is the workshop that makes it all click.

Tap into your creativity with a straightforward, light-heated approach to painting, alongside award-winning watercolor artist Broderick Wong. www.broderickwongart.com

Students are required to bring their own supplies. Each workshop is designed around a minimalist set up and very accessible materials. A concise supply list of 4 pigments, 3 brushes and watercolor paper will be emailed to the registrants.

activities.title: Food Safe - Level One
activities.description: In this same-day certification course, learn about why food poisonings occur and how to prevent them. This course is taught by a certified public health inspector who will share amazing real-life restaurant inspection stories full of the best and worst examples of food handling imaginable! Please bring a pencil and a lunch.

activities.title: Pickleball Lessons: 2 Skills and Drills (Nov/Int)
activities.description:
The next step after Stage 1: “Learn to Play.” Designed for beginner to mid-level players, this class refines strokes and shot selection while teaching third shot, drive, block, smash, lob, and proper court movement. All equipment is provided.
Mona is a certified professional instructor of the IPTPA (International Pickleball Teaching Professional Association) as well as course facilitator for Pickleball Canada’s Coaching Education program. She currently coaches players of all ages; skill levels teaching specific strokes; strategies; shot selections; providing feedback to improve. She is an active member of the VPA (Vancouver Pickleball Association).

activities.title: Pickleball Lessons: 2 Let's Volley (Nov/Int)
activities.description:
This class will focus on one of the most important skills in Pickleball - The volley. Learn proper technique, blocking, control. placement & how to do put-away volleys. We're going to have fun applying pressure while staying in control. Expect lots of action and practice! It is NOT necessary to purchase a paddle for this class. Paddles, balls & equipment will be provided. If you are unable to make the first day, please contact Coach Mona at 778-908-2878.
Mona is a certified professional instructor of the IPTPA (International Pickleball Teaching Professional Association) as well as course facilitator for Pickleball Canada’s Coaching Education program. She currently coaches players of all ages; skill levels teaching specific strokes; strategies; shot selections; providing feedback to improve. She is an active member of the VPA (Vancouver Pickleball Association).

activities.title: Pickleball Lessons: 2 First 4 Shots (Nov/Int)
activities.description:
The first 4 shots sets the stage for everything that follows. In this class, you'll learn the purpose of each shot & how to use them to gain control of the point. We'll cover the serve, return, 3rd & 4th shot, focusing on shot selection, positioning and strategy. It is NOT necessary to purchase a paddle for this class. Paddles, balls & equipment will be provided. If you are unable to make the first day, please contact Coach Mona at 778-908-2878.
Mona is a certified professional instructor of the IPTPA (International Pickleball Teaching Professional Association) as well as course facilitator for Pickleball Canada’s Coaching Education program. She currently coaches players of all ages; skill levels teaching specific strokes; strategies; shot selections; providing feedback to improve. She is an active member of the VPA (Vancouver Pickleball Association).

activities.title: Taking Strides Adaptive Sport
activities.description: Taking Strides offers accessible sports programs with one-on-one support for children with any disability! Our goal is to build physical literacy and teamwork skills through adaptive games including hockey, badminton, relay races, soccer, parachute activities, and so much more! At sessions, kids have the opportunity to connect one-on-one with their paired volunteer and join a supportive community of kids with disabilities in Vancouver. Our sessions are personalized to fit each child’s needs to grow their skill set while having fun! Please let us know how we can best support your child by contacting us at vancouver@takingstrides.org. For more information about our organization and mission, please visit vancouver.takingstrides.org.

activities.title: Hearing Screenings
activities.description:
FREE HEARING SCREENING
Get Clarity About Your Hearing Health in 15 Minutes
Hearing loss often happens gradually and can affect your communication, brain health, and quality of life. The good news? A quick and simple hearing screening can provide the answers you need to take control of your hearing health.
What You Can Expect:
Quick and Easy: A 15-minute screening to assess your hearing.
Professional Expertise: Conducted by Dr. Katarina Vavrovicova, a registered audiologist with years of experience.
Personalized Results: Understand your hearing and receive tailored recommendations for next steps.
Why It’s Important:
Your hearing is essential to staying connected and keeping your brain healthy. Early detection of hearing loss can prevent further complications and improve your overall well-being.
REGISTRATION REQUIRED
To ensure we can accommodate you, please register in advance for your free 15-minute hearing screening. Take charge of your hearing health today—register now and prioritize your well-being!
Offered by Dr. Katarina Vavrovicova, Registered Audiologist at Echo Hearing Care

activities.title: Mobility and Stretching for Seniors
activities.description: This class is taught in Mandarin or Cantonese. Based on a variety of influences such as Tai Chi, Taekwondo focusing on stretching and mobility. Immerse yourself in the grace movements of these ancient martial arts, promoting balance of mind and body. Participants will have improved flexibility, reduced stress, and enhanced well-being. $2.38+tax/drop-in, if space. No session Sep 23, 30, Nov 11.

activities.title: Tai Chi and Health Qigong
activities.description: For more than two thousand years, The Arts of Health Qigong and Tai Chi have enhanced the health of many people. It is now clinically proven that internal organs, exterior muscle joints and mental focus can be significantly strengthened through practice of these arts. Suitable for people of all ages. The instructor, Sifu Lisa Low, is officially recognized as a Master Instructor by the International Health Qigong Federation, an organization that is comprised of thousands of members from 54 countries. $7+tax/drop-in if space. No session Oct 12.

activities.title: Mah Jong - Sunday Drop-in
activities.description: Come with your friends or on your own to meet new people and play Mah Jong together! Table & pieces are included. Experience is required as this will be non instructional. 4 tables will be available on a first come first served basis.

activities.title: Hatha Yoga
activities.description: For people who have moderate experience doing Yoga and are looking to build on previous class work. We work on moderate to intermediate poses to relieve you from muscle pain and stiffness, to improve circulation and overall better health. Many students find they sleep better at night and have increased energy levels during the day. Please note participants are recommended to bring their own yoga mats and other equipment.

activities.title: Seniors Yoga for Flexibility and Strength
activities.description:
Gentle movement and stretching through beginner yoga poses can reduce swelling in joints while increasing joint mobility and improving balance which helps in reducing falls. $9+tax/drop-in if space.

Please note participants are recommended to bring their own yoga mats and other equipment.

No session Oct 12.

activities.title: Seniors Yoga for Flexibility and Strength
activities.description:
The class is designed specifically for seniors seeking improved mobility, balance, and muscle tone. Our gentle yoga routines focus on enhancing flexibility and building strength at a comfortable pace. Perfect for all fitness levels, this class promotes relaxation while supporting your health and vitality. $9+tax/drop-in if space.

Please note participants are recommended to bring their own yoga mats and other equipment.

activities.title: Inclusive Yoga & Sound Bath
activities.description: Gentle Yoga with Sound Bath is an inclusive movement + meditation experience created to meet you where you are. You'll be guided to explore gentle stretches, supported restorative postures, and mindful breathing, suitable for all levels. The practice closes with a guided sound bath meditation using various instruments including crystal sound bowls, koshi chimes, ocean drum and more. This experience is open to all bodies and experience levels, with an emphasis on moving in a way that feels supportive, comfortable, and personal to you. Please bring a yoga mat, all other props will be provided. Drop ins $20, space permitting.

activities.title: Sound Bath Meditation
activities.description: A meditation experience designed to explore slowing down, grounding, and nervous system care through sound. Participants are invited to rest comfortably while being immersed in soothing sounds and vibrations created from instruments such as singing bowls, chimes, drums and other meditative sound tools. This class offers space to pause, reconnect, and rest without expectation. You are welcome to sit, stretch or lie down in whatever way feels most supportive for your body. No experience is needed, and all bodies, backgrounds, and experience levels are welcome. Please bring a yoga mat, pillow and blanket for the most supportive experience. Drop ins $25, space permitting.

activities.title: Pilates
activities.description: This class begins with breath and stillness, to calm and balance the nervous system, softening the outer body in order to sense the inner body, our fluid center or core. We then progress into the structure of Pilates to train and strengthen the core, so that we move more fluidly from our center, helping to organize our mind body experience so that we move with less effort in our lives. $14.29+tax/drop-in if space. No session Oct 12

activities.title: Jump Rope Remix
activities.description:
Remix your cardio routine with just a jump rope! Beginner-friendly, musically driven classes taught by Jumping Jacqz, Jump Rope Coach, NASM-certified Group Fitness Instructor, and cofounder of the Jump Rope Vancouver meetup community. Jump Rope Remix is a signature, rhythm-first jump rope class designed to help people of all skill levels build cardio, coordination, and movement confidence through footwork, music, and play. Join us for a jump rope cardio party with fun footwork & combos and unlock movement skills you can take anywhere. This 55-minute class is taught for all levels in a supportive environment that meets you where you’re at, with options, progressions, and breaks throughout. Bring your own jump rope or borrow one for class. Jump in, remix cardio, and make it something to look forward to! Drop-in $19
No Class Oct 11 & Oct 25.

We encourage participants to bring their own mat.
Drop-in $12.50, space permitting. No class Sept 30.Vienna Luke is a certified Mat Pilates Instructor - completing her certification through A La Ligne Method, (All Method).

activities.description:
Dive deeper into the foundations and movement principles of this beautiful traditional dance from the Dominican Republic. Para hockey for Beginners. Everyone is welcome to participate - all players will be required to be in a sled

This session is open to people aged 8+ years who are new to sledge or just want to improve their basic skills. Learn how to maneuver the sled, cut edges, make tape-to-tape passes, take wicked shots and engage in team plays. Test out your skills in a fun scrimmage at the end of each session. A part of the ice may be dedicated to just skating.

Equipment: A CSA approved hockey helmet with a full cage, hockey gloves and elbow pads are required. Chest protector and shin guards are strongly recommended. Equipment provided on a first-come, first-served basis.

All Hockey Programs are co-ed and participants must sign a waiver at the beginning of each session.

All registered participants must check in with the attendant up to 5 minutes after the program start time. Failure to do so may result in the spot being forfeited to a waiting player.

*Monthly Flexipass and 10-Visit passes are accepted for this program.

activities.title: Pickleball - Learning the Basics
activities.description: Discover why pickleball is the fastest-growing sport in North America! This beginner-friendly, progressive class will introduce you to the rules, scoring, equipment, and fundamental skills of the game, including serving, returning, volleying, and dinking. Through guided instruction and fun on-court drills, you’ll build confidence, improve coordination, and learn basic court positioning. Perfect for those who are brand new to the game or looking to refresh their skills before joining drop-in play. If you have a paddle, please bring it, otherwise a limited number of paddles will be available on loan for each class.

activities.title: Pickleball - Live Coaching and Play - Beginner +
activities.description:
Take your pickleball skills to the next level! Perfect for those who have completed a beginner class or have some playing experience and are ready for more! This class focuses on improving consistency, shot placement, and game strategy.
You’ll refine your serve and return, practice controlled dinks and volleys, and learn how to set up winning plays through better court positioning and movement. Real-time coaching during drills and game play will help you build confidence and prepare for more competitive play. If you have a paddle, please bring it, otherwise a limited number of paddles will be available on loan for each class.
This class is designed for players who are progressing from Beginner level and are still developing consistency in foundational skills. Participants who have previously completed multiple sessions of Beginner Plus and demonstrate consistent rallying, serve, return, and transition skills are encouraged to register in an Intermediate level class moving forward.
No class Oct 12.

activities.title: Hearing Screenings
activities.description:
FREE HEARING SCREENING
Get Clarity About Your Hearing Health in 15 Minutes
Hearing loss often happens gradually and can affect your communication, brain health, and quality of life. The good news? A quick and simple hearing screening can provide the answers you need to take control of your hearing health.
What You Can Expect:
Quick and Easy: A 15-minute screening to assess your hearing.
Professional Expertise: Conducted by Dr. Katarina Vavrovicova, a registered audiologist with years of experience.
Personalized Results: Understand your hearing and receive tailored recommendations for next steps.
Why It’s Important:
Your hearing is essential to staying connected and keeping your brain healthy. Early detection of hearing loss can prevent further complications and improve your overall well-being.
REGISTRATION REQUIRED
To ensure we can accommodate you, please register in advance for your free 15-minute hearing screening. Take charge of your hearing health today—register now and prioritize your well-being!
Offered by Dr. Katarina Vavrovicova, Registered Audiologist at Echo Hearing Care

activities.title: False Creek Youth Concession (Friday Volunteers)
activities.description:
Come join this leadership team to give back to our False Creek neighborhood while connecting with new people and gaining skills such as notetaking, budgeting, public speaking, etc. Participants will have the opportunity to practice their skills through planning activities for other youth, implementing their own community projects, assisting with special events and taking part in workshops. This is a great way to achieve volunteer hours and/or work experience! Volunteers will be provided with an hour log and are responsible for tracking their own hours volunteered. *NO SESSION MAY 16*
*Please note: participants who do not show up for the first two sessions without providing notice will be automatically removed from the program to make space for others*
activities.ageText: Age at least 13 yrs but less than 18 yrs

activities.title: False Creek Youth Volunteers
activities.description:
Looking to earn volunteer hours, build valuable work experience, and make a difference in your community? This hands-on volunteer program focuses on supporting day-to-day projects and completing meaningful tasks that help our programs and events run smoothly, rather than leadership or event planning. Volunteers tasks may include creating promotional materials, distributing them in the community, decorating the centre, assisting with special events and kitchen programs, running the Saturday concession, organizing supplies, and participating in community clean-ups. It’s a great opportunity to develop practical skills, connect with others, and make a positive impact in your community.
Note there is no session on October 10.
Extended volunteer sessions for special events will be:October 31 – 9:30am to 1:00pmDecember 12 – 9:30am to 1:00pm
*Please note: participants who do not show up for the first two sessions without providing notice will be automatically removed from the program to make space for others*

activities.title: Chinese Classical Dance
activities.description: Chinese classical dance is filled with rich culture and splendid form. Haiyan Zhang wishes to share the beauty of Chinese and other different cultural dances for everyone to enjoy. Dance forms includes: traditional Chinese, Tibetan, XinJiang, Mongolian, Korean, and more! This course is led with traditional movements explained in Mandarin. Understanding of the Mandarin language an asset but not necessary for participation.

activities.title: Smart Device Workshop for Seniors
activities.description:
Are you having troubles with your smart devices (Apple or Android), or simply want to learn more of the functionality behind it? Bring in your questions on a piece of paper and be partnered with our very own local high school students to guide and explain your smart device. They can also show you simple tips and tricks on your device if you don't have any questions.
Note: Phones and tablets are preferred. Youth have limited knowledge with laptops. Don't forget to bring paper and pen to write everything you learned and come back with your written questions on your next visit! :)

activities.title: Pilates: Intermediate Beyond the Basics
activities.description: Join our Pilates community and take your practice beyond the basics! This 50-minute intermediate class builds on the fundamental movement principles of Pilates, incorporating more challenging exercises, sequences, and movement patterns. Build strength, stability, balance, coordination, flexibility, and body awareness through a dynamic full-body workout. We’ll focus on six key Pilates principles: breathing, concentration, centering, control, precision, and flow. Modifications will be offered to support individual needs and abilities.New participants: Please arrive 10 minutes early for your first class to complete the required medical information and waiver. Drop in $25.

activities.title: Woodworking Studio Session Time
activities.description:
Registration only.
Woodworking Studio Session Times are available for those who have completed Woodworking: Level 1 at the Roundhouse Community Arts & Recreation Centre. Also available to those who can demonstrate considerable knowledge and experience of woodworking with approval from Jeremy Tomlinson of Urban Woodworker. Please contact the Roundhouse Community Arts & Recreation Centre front desk if you have any questions.
Registration closes 24 hours before the posted date and time. No refunds within 24 of the posted start date and time. Registrations accepted over the phone and in person within 24 hours of the posted start date and time if another participant is registered.

activities.title: Woodworking Studio Time - Wood Turning Specific
activities.description:
Registration only.
Woodworking Studio Session Times are available for those who have completed Woodworking Level 1 Wood Turning at the Roundhouse Community Arts & Recreation Centre. Also available to those who can demonstrate considerable knowledge and experience of woodworking with approval from Jeremy Tomlinson of Urban Woodworker. Please contact the Roundhouse Community Arts & Recreation Centre front desk if you have any questions.
Registration closes 24 hours before the posted date and time. No refunds within 24 of the posted start date and time. Registrations accepted over the phone and in person within 24 hours of the posted start date and time if another participant is registered.
This studio time is open to approved users for either regular woodworking projects or wood turning however it’s wood turning specific. Therefore woodworking projects that are not wood turning must be small as space is limited when wood lathes are in the studio.
There are no refunds for woodworkers who are not turners, who are dissatisfied with the available space after arriving at the studio.
For the most part the machines such as jointer, planer and table saw will be unused during these studio times since wood turners will be using the lathes.
Please contact the Roundhouse Community Arts & Recreation Centre front desk for any questions.

activities.title: Aquafit - Shallow Moderate
activities.description:
Shallow aquafit

This 50-minute Aquafit class is imbedded in a 90-minute Swim Session. Aquafit is a moderately paced and energizing class that utilizes water resistance for a variety of exercise combinations with warm up, cardio, strength, stretch and cool down components, designed for participants who want to increase their fitness and muscular endurance.
Hot Tub access is limited and is first come first serve. Recommended maximum of 10 minutes. Saunas and steam rooms are not available at all locations.
Please call the facility for more details.

activities.title: Youth Badminton Drop-in
activities.description:
All levels welcome!

Sessions are supervised by a Youth Program Assistant I/II or Community Youth Worker, but there is no instructor for this program.
All badminton lesson players must register for the badminton drop-in session and cannot stay after lessons unless registered!

Please note the session can accommodate up to 20 players maximum. REGISTRATION IS REQUIRED. Registration open 1 day in advance at 12:00pm. Please check-in with a Youth Staff upon arrival.

There will be a waitlist on the day of, please speak to a youth staff to write your name down. The waitlist is not guaranteed.

Welcome to our youth gym programs at Killarney Community Centre! Looking to get back into the game and tune up your skills? Youth staff will help organize games and rotations. Please note the following rules to be followed in the gymnasium:

How to Play:

  • Competition is permitted
  • Wash your hands before and after play
  • No food or drink in the gymnasium
  • Use appropriate and respectful language.
  • Respect the equipment (volleyballs, nets, etc.).
  • Respect direction from Killarney staff and be kind to other youth.

If you have any further inquiries, please call the Killarney Youth Office at 604-718-8212.

activities.title: Journey Basketball: Junior Ballers (6-8yrs)
activities.description:
Beginner: Recommended age is 6-8 years.Journey Basketball for 6- to 8-year-olds is an engaging and educational initiative designed to introduce young athletes to the fundamentals of basketball. Through a mix of interactive drills, fun exercises, and skill-building activities, this program aims to instill a strong foundation in dribbling, shooting, passing, and basic game strategies. With an emphasis on fostering teamwork, sportsmanship, and a love for the game, our experienced coaches guide participants through a supportive and encouraging environment, ensuring each child develops their skills while enjoying the sport.
Participants are encouraged to bring their own usable basketball if they have one, but will be provided a basketball for the session if they don't.

If you have any further inquiries, please contact the Killarney Youth Office at 604-718-8212

No class on Statutory Holidays

activities.title: Aquafit - Shallow Moderate
activities.description:
Shallow aquafit

This 50-minute Aquafit class is imbedded in a 90-minute Swim Session. Aquafit is a moderately paced and energizing class that utilizes water resistance for a variety of exercise combinations with warm up, cardio, strength, stretch and cool down components, designed for participants who want to increase their fitness and muscular endurance.
Hot Tub access is limited and is first come first serve. Recommended maximum of 10 minutes. Saunas and steam rooms are not available at all locations.
Please call the facility for more details.

NOTE: The nature of the activity is such that you may interact with other people who are considered to be in good health, continuous physical distance between other people cannot be guaranteed, and, by participating in the activity, you are at risk of being infected by a pathogen, including but not limited to SARS-COV-2. SARS-COV-2, which causes the disease COVID-19, may exacerbate other health issues and is the cause of an ongoing global pandemic. SARS-COV-2 is highly communicable and dangerous. If you become infected with SARS-COV2, you may transmit it to other people even if you are not exhibiting symptoms of illness.

Proof Of Vaccination

• Effective September 13, people will need to show proof of vaccination to get into certain programs, events, and services at this facility.

Exemptions are in place for children and youth programs and activities. Adults 22+ will need to show proof of vaccination. (Young people 12+ will need proof of vaccination for fitness centres and weight room facilities.)

For acceptable proof of vaccination and for all other information, please cut and paste into your web browser: https://www2.gov.bc.ca/vaccinecard.html.

• It is recommended that you arrive early for your activity in order to show proof of vaccination if required.

Communicable Disease Health & Safety Practices

• Participants are required to comply with the current Face Coverings Order of the Provincial Health Officer. For more information, please cut and paste into your web browser: https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/covid-19/info/restrictions

• Participants should assess themselves daily for symptoms of common cold, influenza, COVID-19, or other infectious respiratory disease before attending a program.

• Participants who are ill, including participants of essential service providers, should not attend a program or access the Community Centre. If you are unsure, you should self-isolate and contact 8-1-1 or the local public health unit.

• Registration and payment is required for most programs to help reduce the capacity to allow for physical distancing. Limited drop-ins may be permitted, depending on the facility.

• All participants are encouraged to practice proper hand hygiene and respiratory etiquette by covering coughs or sneezes.

activities.title: Killarney 1on1 Personal Training Sessions
activities.description:
Book your time slot now for a 1-on-1 Personal Training session with Killarney’s very own Personal Trainers. Killarney's certified fitness professional will work with you to identify your goals and create a specific customized program that maximizes the benefits of your training routine. Personal Training Packages include the option of 1, 3, 5 or 10 1-hour sessions.

Multi Session Fees:

1 Session $58.17

3 Sessions $161.20

5 Sessions $259.27

10 Sessions $465.43

Prices do not include GST

For more information or if your looking to book a session, email your request to killarneyfitnesscentre@vancouver.ca. We will get back to you within 48 hours.

*Before your first session, download & complete the following Required KFC Personal Training Forms:

*Killarney Fitness Centre Consent & Release

*A Personal Trainer Health & Fitness Questionnaire

*A Physical Activity Readiness Questionnaire form (PAR-Q+)

*If you are pregnant: PARmed-X

*If you answered “YES” to any of the questions on the PAR-Q+ form, a note from your doctor or physiotherapist is required. The note must confirm that you can proceed with fitness training.

REQUIRED KFC Personal Training Forms LINK

Email your forms to killarneyfitnesscentre@vancouver.ca or submit your forms to the Killarney Community Centre reception desk 48hours prior to your first 1on1 Personal Training Session.

activities.title: Collage and Mixed Media: Cut, Paste & Create
activities.description:
Come make art, meet new friends, and enjoy the playful freedom of collage! This hands-on, social workshop invites you to cut, tear, layer, and combine an unexpected mix of images and materials while chatting, experimenting, and having fun.
Collage is one of the most generous and accessible forms of art-making. Your materials can be almost anything—from magazines, colourful papers and fabric to old photographs, postcards, tickets and treasures rescued from the recycling bin. Using scissors, glue, or simply tearing paper by hand, you’ll discover how easily everyday materials can be transformed into expressive and imaginative artwork.
We’ll explore a variety of collage techniques, from recognizable imagery to abstract compositions, while learning about the fascinating history of collage and its evolution as an important contemporary art practice.
Most importantly, this is a space to play, experiment, connect, and express yourself. No previous art experience is necessary. Individual guidance and encouragement are provided throughout, helping you develop your ideas and discover your own creative voice.
Come sift through an abundance of images and materials, find your treasures, and see where your imagination takes you. All skill levels welcome!
Supply List is available on registration email Faye: nsyffayerman@gmail.com

activities.description: A beginner class open to all who want to stay active and have fun with Chinese songs and music. activities.title: Iyengar Yoga
activities.description: Are you keen to improve your flexibility, strength and awareness of your body? Then this class is for you. The Iyengar method focuses on alignment, mobility, longer holds and moving your body with precision and mindfulness. Iyengar yoga uses many props such as belts, bricks, chairs and bolsters making poses accessible to all body shapes, sizes and capabilities. Iyengar yoga is designed to take beginners through a series of movements building towards more advanced poses. It is thus perfect for those with stiff bodies, who can't sit on the floor or aren't keen on energetic workout classes. Drop in permitted if space is available.

KBL is a self refereed coed basketball league that plays on Sundays between 1 pm and 5 pm at Sunset, 1 pm - 9 pm at Kitsilano and Kerrisdale community centres. There are three divisions. activities.title: Beginner Flamenco Workshop
activities.description: Introducing you to the art of flamenco through diverse rhythms, footwork, arm work, and simple choreographies. activities.title: Therapeutic Art for Seniors Free Workshop
activities.description: Join us for a free therapeutic art workshop designed especially for seniors. Explore creativity, self-expression, and connection in a welcoming, supportive environment. No previous art experience is needed. Enjoy a guided art activity, gentle conversation, and the opportunity to discover the joy of making art together. No previous art experience is required, and all materials are provided. Come as you are, meet new people, and enjoy a relaxing creative experience. This workshop is free, but registration is required.

activities.title: Living Streets - WALKtober Seniors' Walk
activities.description: Join us for a community walk hosted by BEST Mobility as part of the WALKtober campaign under the Living Streets program. These walks aim to promote walking as an active, sustainable, and inclusive mode of transportation while fostering social connection among participants with routes accessible for all ages and abilities. Registration required for this free event and a waiver must be filled out before the walk. Please meet at the Kerrisdale Seniors Centre.

Hot Tub access is limited and is first come first serve. Recommended maximum of 10 minutes. Saunas and steam rooms are not available at all locations.

Maximum capacity is 36 participants. Pre-registration via online, phone-in, or in-person opens 3 days prior to the session date at 12pm. Pre-registration closes 30-minutes prior to session start. Limited drop-in spots available; pre-registration is encouraged.

Wristbands required to be worn when participating in the class.

Please call the facility for more details.

activities.description:
All levels welcome!

Sessions are supervised by a Youth Program Assistant I/II or Community Youth Worker, but there is no instructor for this program.

Please note the session can accommodate up to 36 players maximum. REGISTRATION IS REQUIRED. Registration open 1 day in advance at 12:00pm. Please check-in with a Youth Staff upon arrival.

There will be a waitlist on the day of, please speak to a youth staff to write your name down. The waitlist is not guaranteed. If you are not here within 15minutes, your spot will be given up to the waitlist participants

Welcome to our youth gym programs at Killarney Community Centre! Looking to get back into the game and tune up your skills? Come by to bump, set, and spike! Youth staff will help organize games and rotations. Please note the following rules to be followed in the gymnasium:

How to Play:

  • Competition is permitted
  • Wash your hands before and after play
  • No food or drink in the gymnasium
  • Use appropriate and respectful language.
  • Respect the equipment (volleyballs, nets, etc.).
  • Respect direction from Killarney staff and be kind to other youth.

If you have any further inquiries, please call the Killarney Youth Office at 604-718-8212.

activities.description:
Space Permitting - Drop-in $3
This open gym time is for individuals with complex disabilities and their support workers to socialize and relax in a safe, calm community space. Participants are welcome to use the space to exercise and connect with one another in a low stimulus environment.
For more information about this opportunity please contact: Recreation Programmer @ Killarney Community Centre 604-718-6259 or email access.services@vancouver.ca. Max participants: 6 (+ 6 attendants).

Activity Drop-in Policy

Drop-ins are accepted in programs where stated “Space Permitting - Drop-in fees”… Drop-in patrons can purchase their spot 15 minutes prior to program start time in person ONLY, based on 1st come 1st served. IMPORTANT: If maximum program capacity has already been met with registered patrons no drop-ins will be permitted, regardless of no-show patrons.
